stem: A job is scheduled every fifteen minutes, but one afternoon a run takes almost an hour. The team reviews the history afterwards and has to account for what became of the triggers that fired while the long run was still going.

option_texts.A: They were skipped, because only a single run of a job can be active at a time
option_texts.B: They were queued and replayed in order once the long run finally finished
option_texts.C: They started in parallel, because a schedule is independent of any run in flight
option_texts.D: They failed and were recorded as errors against the schedule that produced them

drill_answer_short: By default only one run of a job is active at a time, and runs from most trigger types are skipped beyond that limit
decision_hinge: By default only a single run of a job can be active at a time, and runs from most trigger types are skipped when they exceed the configured max concurrency for a job.

plausible_options.B: account for what became of the triggers that fired while the long run was still going

eliminated_by.C: A job is scheduled every fifteen minutes
eliminated_by.D: The team reviews the history afterwards

distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling - job completion triggers do retain a ready completion, but a schedule does not queue
distractor_traps.C: T5: common misconception - concurrency is capped at one run unless the limit is raised
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - a skipped trigger is not recorded as a failure

stem: An ingest stream started on the simpler discovery method, and the directory has since grown enough that the team wants the other one. They must know what moving across costs them in correctness when the stream is restarted.

option_texts.A: A full reprocess, because the new mode has no record of the files already taken
option_texts.B: Nothing, because the mode can be switched across restarts with exactly-once still held
option_texts.C: Possible duplicates, because progress does not carry across the two mechanisms
option_texts.D: A new target table, because a stream cannot change how it discovers its input

drill_answer_short: You can switch file discovery modes across stream restarts and still get exactly-once processing
decision_hinge: Auto Loader supports two modes for detecting new files, directory listing and file notification, and you can switch file discovery modes across stream restarts and still obtain exactly-once data processing guarantees.

plausible_options.C: what moving across costs them in correctness when the stream is restarted

eliminated_by.A: the directory has since grown enough that the team wants the other one
eliminated_by.D: An ingest stream started on the simpler discovery method

distractor_traps.A: T5: common misconception - the checkpoint survives the switch, so nothing is re-read
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling - progress lives in the checkpoint rather than in either discovery mechanism
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - the discovery mode is a stream option and is meant to be changed

stem: A new team member asks why the design moves records through three named tiers rather than loading the source straight into the tables that analysts query. The reviewer wants the answer framed in terms of what each hop is for.

option_texts.A: Each hop belongs to a different team, so the tiers mirror the organisation chart
option_texts.B: Each hop stores the same records again so a failure in one tier can be rolled back
option_texts.C: Each hop incrementally improves the structure and quality of the data as it flows
option_texts.D: Each hop uses a different file format, so the tiers trade storage against speed

drill_answer_short: The medallion pattern incrementally and progressively improves the structure and quality of data across Bronze, Silver and Gold
decision_hinge: A medallion architecture is a data design pattern whose goal is to incrementally and progressively improve the structure and quality of data as it flows through each layer, from Bronze to Silver to Gold layer tables.

plausible_options.B: why the design moves records through three named tiers

eliminated_by.A: The reviewer wants the answer framed in terms of what each hop is for
eliminated_by.D: rather than loading the source straight into the tables that analysts query

distractor_traps.A: T1: fabricated - the tiers are stages of refinement, not an ownership split
distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling - the tiers do retain earlier copies, but recovery is not the purpose of the pattern
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - the layers are not distinguished by file format

stem: A reviewer is checking whether a proposed tier is drawn correctly. The proposal holds a handful of curated tables such as customer spending and an executive summary, and it is the surface business users read.

option_texts.A: It is the Bronze tier, which keeps the raw state of each source in its original form
option_texts.B: It is the Silver tier, which holds validated detail for business analysts to work through
option_texts.C: It is a serving cache, which sits outside the pattern and is rebuilt on each query
option_texts.D: It is the Gold tier, designed for business users and holding fewer datasets than the rest

drill_answer_short: The Gold layer is designed for business users and contains fewer datasets than silver and bronze
decision_hinge: The Gold layer is designed for business users and contains fewer datasets than silver and bronze, holding highly aggregated information such as a business summary for the executive staff.

plausible_options.B: a handful of curated tables such as customer spending and an executive summary

eliminated_by.A: it is the surface business users read
eliminated_by.C: A reviewer is checking whether a proposed tier is drawn correctly

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - raw original-format records are the Bronze tier, two hops below
distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling - Silver keeps the detail, where this proposal is aggregated and small
distractor_traps.C: T1: fabricated - no serving cache tier exists in the pattern

stem: A partitioned table is being moved onto the newer layout feature, and the team runs the alter statement without naming any columns at all. They want to predict which columns the table ends up organised by.

option_texts.A: The current partition columns, which become the new clustering columns
option_texts.B: Every column, because an unspecified list means the whole row is used
option_texts.C: None, because the statement is rejected until a column list is supplied
option_texts.D: The primary key columns, which the platform falls back to when none are named

drill_answer_short: With no options specified the statement uses the current partition columns as the new clustering columns
decision_hinge: With no options specified, the statement uses the current partition columns as the new clustering columns.

plausible_options.C: runs the alter statement without naming any columns at all

eliminated_by.B: They want to predict which columns the table ends up organised by
eliminated_by.D: A partitioned table is being moved onto the newer layout feature

distractor_traps.B: T1: fabricated - clustering on every column is never the default
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling - the bare form is valid precisely because a sensible default exists
distractor_traps.D: T5: common misconception - a primary key is informational and is not a layout input
